tickets.objective: Capture the matched RT64 CPU/GPU render baseline: route, snapshot/report/API-identity seams, and a fresh-process five-pair counterbalanced runner.
findings: fn64-abi exposes an owned raw frame-census measurement snapshot; fn64-certification builds typed control and explicit-partial development reports.
The headless route runs Shell::pump_one_frame outside the winit/pixels compositor; five counterbalanced control/instrumented pairs launch as fresh processes.
A control run can become comparison_ready only after the post-create verifier completes and both horizon endpoint observations are available and unchanged.
No real matched baseline has been recorded; the private linked-build and native-identity gates remain open.

This is an open evidence gap, not a stall: the C-program receipt and native device query have no linked private-game validation, so no real matched baseline exists yet. It blocks the performance/parity claim, not independent implementation, so the ticket remains RUNNING rather than BLOCKED.
tickets.next_action: Exercise the C-RecompiledFuncs receipt and native identity query against a clean private linked build, then run five independent unprofiled repetitions plus counterbalanced instrumented controls on the declared route.

tickets.objective: Generate the machine-checked RT64 source/task denominator: assign every allowed project-owned host/shader module a milestone, workstream, port state, evidence state, and exclusive task-card owner.
findings: The dual-pin inventory schema fn64.rt64-port-inventory.v2 records 276 files across the included prefixes with per-file oracle/port digests, include edges, and non-exhaustive declaration/definition hints.
6 files are modified between the oracle and accepted port-source commits; 270 are unchanged; 0 added or removed.
Every file carries a task_card with id/outcome/authority/owner_lane/recommended_profile/writable_paths/non_goals/baseline_command/exit_gate/evidence_state/claim_status.
tickets.next_action: Dispatch disjoint decode, TMEM, framebuffer, and GPU-probe task cards from the merged checked denominator.

tickets.objective: Land the fn64-render-ir ownership spine: owned lifetime, FullSync ordering, DRAM/XBUS raw-command separation, resource journals, and move-only decode/submission/completion/commit transitions.
findings: The first candidate was rejected because tickets self-issued completion/commit authority, CMD_END/FullSync/interrupt order was lossy, installed memory bounds were erased, aggregate bounds were unsafe, journal effects were contradictory, and hostile records could allocate before validation.

The accepted crate separates queue/completion/guest-commit capabilities, uses effect-bearing receipts, preserves exact command and DP observation sequences and installed memory layout, enforces aggregate bounds and a strict resource-purpose matrix, and preflights hostile record geometry before allocation.

Independent review, strict clippy, documentation lint, compile-fail tests, and the 10-run deterministic bar are closed. Cross-crate placement of those authorities is intentionally tracked by M1.2 rather than hidden inside this crate.
tickets.next_action: Place the three capabilities with their real queue/backend/guest-memory owners and exercise the cross-crate lifecycle in M1.2.

tickets.objective: Run the primary-platform Metal hard-feature probe on pinned wgpu 30: adapter identity, dual-source blending, texture-array access, required formats, timestamps, submission ordering, and bounded fallback classification.
findings: The selected probe baseline is direct wgpu 30.0.0 rather than the shell's transitive wgpu 0.19 stack.
Raw capability and semantics probes are independent of M1; only the later submission-ticket lifecycle integration depends on M1.1.

The Apple M5 Pro runtime receipt advertises every required hard-feature row, including partially-bound binding arrays, while optional timestamp writes inside encoders and passes are absent. These are adapter advertisements plus a basic copy/readback execution, not semantic parity claims.
tickets.next_action: Execute the advertised capability-specific semantic, format-I/O, submission, coverage, and surface cards before classifying portability or fallback policy.

tickets.objective: Build the canonical strict status/ticket manifest and a dependency-free Python generator/validator rendering a terminal view, generated Markdown, and a self-contained responsive local HTML workflow dashboard.
findings: The manifest and schema are new and separate from docs/rt64-port-inventory.json (per-file source denominator) and docs/rt64-port-authority.json (license/source pin); this ticket adds the missing per-ticket workflow layer the plan's status capsule currently only carries as prose.

States are restricted to the exact orchestration-doc vocabulary (READY/RUNNING/READY_FOR_REVIEW/BLOCKED/REJECTED/INTEGRATED for tickets; PLANNED/READY/IN PROGRESS/BLOCKED/COMPLETE for milestones); the generator never infers a state from code presence.
--serve binds 127.0.0.1 only, refuses any other bind host, and serves only the generated dashboard directory read-only.
tickets.next_action: Keep ticket states, blockers, run counts, and retrospectives current as each reviewed branch merges or rebases.

retrospective.friction: The plan/orchestration docs carry per-ticket fields (id, profile, model, dependencies, writable_paths, state) only as prose in a status capsule and handoff template, so a session must re-read the whole plan file to reconstruct current ticket state.
retrospective.cause: No single machine-checked file previously owned the ticket-level denominator; docs/rt64-port-inventory.json owns per-source-file task cards, not per-ticket workflow state.
retrospective.prevention: This manifest and its --check validator give future sessions one strict, mechanically checked ticket table instead of re-deriving it from prose; validation now rejects review-ready claims before every declared run bar is met.

tickets.objective: Land the backend-neutral conformance ladder: one typed fixture contract, RT64 FFI and Rust delegates, proof-bearing receipts, exact row-state denominator, mutation tests, and a deliberately failing port-progress gate.
findings: RT64 is an executable compatibility delegate, not universal correctness authority; known defects use hardware or permitted reference authority.
Ordinary CI must execute every closed row and protect the pending denominator, while port-progress remains nonzero until every required Rust row passes.
tickets.next_action: Prove one RT64 pass, one explicit divergence/unavailable row, one Rust-pending row, and negative receipt mutations end to end on the active clean branch.

tickets.objective: Place IR authority at real crate boundaries: validated ABI capture, distinct queue submission, backend-owned effect completion, and guest-memory-owner commit with rejection leaving no architectural publication.
findings: An ephemeral packet or digest may exist as backend input before success; the prohibited state is a retained receipt, trace record, guest mutation, or architectural observation for rejected or uncommitted work.
The first slice is an executable synthetic mechanism proof around the permitted ReferenceBackend, not a claim that production raw-DPC dispatch has already migrated.
tickets.next_action: Prove success and rejection through distinct owners, then independently review whether the types prevent early completion, cross-authority reuse, duplicate commit, and publication on failure.

tickets.objective: Execute Metal hard-feature semantics and format-I/O fixtures so adapter advertisements become exact behavioral evidence or explicit bounded fallback findings.
findings: Capability bits alone do not close a renderer requirement; each native and fallback path must execute and read back exact bytes.
This ticket owns masks and wrapping arithmetic, TMEM-like addressing, nonuniform arrays, dual-source/manual blending, explicit format conversions, and rejection of unsupported reinterpretation.
tickets.next_action: Run exact native and fallback fixtures for 10 host processes and report unsupported features distinctly from semantic mismatches.
